app.name: DiCE-IFC
app.tagline: A BIM toolkit that never uploads your models
app.description: IFC viewing and federation, georeferencing, IDS authoring and validation, BCF management, and qualified signature with the Cartão de Cidadão. Everything is processed in your browser.
app.metaDescription: Browser-based BIM toolkit: IFC viewing and federation, georeferencing, IDS authoring and validation, BCF management, and qualified signature with the Cartão de Cidadão. Models never leave your device.

privacy.intro: This page is exhaustive on purpose. If DiCE-IFC ever sends something not listed below, that is a bug — please report it.
privacy.localTitle: Stays on your machine, but leaves the tab
privacy.localIntro: A browser cannot reach a smart card, so signing involves one hop out of the tab. It carries a hash and goes no further than loopback.

leaves.when: When you sign in or create an account
leaves.why: Authentication. Nothing else in the app requires an account.

leaves.when: When you open or edit a project
leaves.why: So a team shares the same project list. No model data is attached.

leaves.what: A SHA-256 hash of a file
leaves.when: Only when you request a qualified timestamp (XAdES-T)
leaves.where: A timestamping authority, via this app's API as a CORS proxy
leaves.why: RFC 3161 timestamps prove when a signature existed. A hash cannot be turned back into the file.

leaves.what: Certificate serial numbers and issuer names
leaves.where: OCSP / CRL / EU trusted-list endpoints, via this app's API as a CORS proxy
leaves.why: To check whether a signing certificate was revoked, and whether its issuer is trusted.

leaves.what: An audit row: your user, a timestamp, the file name, the file's hash, and the signing certificate's subject and serial
leaves.when: Only if you explicitly turn on the signature audit log for a project
leaves.why: So a project can show who signed what and when. Off by default. Never includes the file or the signature.

leaves.what: Dictionary search text, and the IFC class names your specification already mentions — IFCWALL, not any value
leaves.when: Only in the IDS editor, and only after you choose a bSDD dictionary. Nothing is selected by default
leaves.where: The buildingSMART Data Dictionary (api.bsdd.buildingsmart.org), via this app's API as a proxy
leaves.why: To suggest the property sets, property names and allowed values a class can carry, so a specification does not silently apply to nothing because of a typo. bSDD sends no CORS headers, so the call goes through this app's API — which also means bSDD sees this deployment's address rather than yours. Lookups fire on a class you have named, not on every keystroke. No model, no IDS file and no property value is sent, and the editor works normally with bSDD unreachable.

leaves.where: The configured tile provider. Self-hosted Protomaps by default, which is this app's own origin; this deployment is configured for OpenFreeMap (tiles.openfreemap.org)
leaves.why: To draw a basemap under the model footprint in georeferencing. Tile requests reveal roughly where you are looking — in this module, that is where the building is — which is why a self-hosted provider is the default. OpenFreeMap needs no account and states that it does not log requests, but it is still a third party. Removing NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_STYLE_URL turns the basemap off; the georeferencing itself does not need it. When a MapTiler key is configured the panel also offers Streets, OpenStreetMap and Satellite from api.maptiler.com; those requests are tied to that account key. The basemap now covers whatever the camera is looking at, so panning and zooming out fetches tiles for the area you move to. Choosing 3D buildings streams 3D geometry from Cesium ion (api.cesium.com and assets.ion.cesium.com) against an ion token; those requests are tied to that token and ion's attribution stays on screen while the tiles are shown.

localOnly.what: A digest of the signature's own metadata — 32 to 64 bytes
localOnly.where: The DiCE-IFC signing companion, on http://127.0.0.1
localOnly.why: The signing key is on your Cartão de Cidadão, and a browser cannot talk to a smart card. The companion passes the digest to the card and returns the signature. It has no endpoint that accepts a document and refuses anything larger than a few kilobytes. Every request must carry a token the companion generates fresh each time it starts, and it hands that token out only to this application's own origin — which is why you never have to copy one, and why another web page cannot use it to drive your card.

never: IFC models — geometry, properties, quantities, classifications, everything
BCF issue sets, comments, viewpoints or snapshots
IDS specifications, whether authored here or imported
Validation results, reports and the entities that failed
Coordinates, control points or georeferencing parameters
Your signature PIN — the Autenticação.gov middleware asks for it, not this app
Your private key — it never leaves the Cartão de Cidadão
The signature value and the signed container
privacy.enforce1: Files are read with the File System Access API or drag-and-drop, parsed by WebAssembly inside Web Workers, cached in the Origin Private File System (a per-site sandbox that no other site and no server can read), and rendered by WebGPU or WebGL. All of that is browser-local by construction.
privacy.enforce2: On top of that, the codebase forbids passing a File, Blob or ArrayBuffer to any network call — a lint rule fails the build if someone tries — and a Content-Security-Policy blocks connections to origins other than this app's own API and the configured map tile provider. Everything else in the table above — timestamps, revocation checks, bSDD — is reached through this app's own API rather than from the tab, so those services never see your browser or your address.
privacy.enforce3: Signing works the same way. The document is hashed in the tab; only the hash of the signature's own metadata is handed to a local companion application, which passes it to the card through the Autenticação.gov middleware. The middleware asks you for the signature PIN directly — this app has no PIN field and never sees one. The signed container is assembled and zipped in the tab and saved straight to your disk.
privacy.enforce4: Clearing site data removes the OPFS cache and every draft stored with it.

signSetup.title: Signing setup
signSetup.description: What has to be installed on this machine before a Cartão de Cidadão can sign.
signSetup.cmdNotSupportedTitle: Chave Móvel Digital is not supported
signSetup.cmdNotSupportedBody: This application signs with the physical Cartão de Cidadão only. Chave Móvel Digital is a remote signing service: using it would mean sending a digest of your model off this machine, which is exactly what this application is built not to do. To sign with CMD, use the official Autenticação.gov desktop application instead.
signSetup.signingCompanionBody: A browser cannot talk to a smart card, so a small local program does it. Install it once; it starts with you and this page pairs with it by itself. There is nothing to copy.
signSetup.noInstallerPublished: No installer is published for this deployment. Build one with companion/packaging/build_macos.sh or build_windows.ps1, or run it from source with pip install ./companion && dice-companion. See companion/packaging/README.md.
signSetup.companionDigestOnly: The companion signs a digest and nothing else — your model never reaches it, and neither does your PIN, which the card middleware asks for in its own window.
signSetup.cardReaderBody: Any CCID reader. A CC v2 can also be read contactlessly, which needs the CAN printed on the card.
signSetup.middlewareBody: Provides pteidpkcs11, the PKCS#11 module that talks to the card. It raises its own PIN window — this application never sees, transports or stores your PIN.
signSetup.extensionBody: A browser cannot reach a smart card: WebCrypto has no token access and WebAuthn cannot drive a qualified signing key. A locally installed companion is unavoidable.
signSetup.statusUnknown: — cannot be detected from the browser
signSetup.noProviderRemedy: No signing provider could be loaded in this browser.

signVerify.title: Verify a signature
signVerify.description: Drop a signed container to re-hash its payload and check the signature. Nothing is uploaded.
signVerify.fileCouldNotBeRead: That file could not be read.
signVerify.signatureValid: Signature valid — the content is exactly what was signed
signVerify.notATrustDecision: This is not a trust decision. It proves the content has not changed since it was signed, and that the signer held the key for the certificate below. Whether that certificate is a genuine Portuguese qualified certificate, and whether it had been revoked, needs the trusted list and an OCSP responder — data a browser cannot fetch directly. That check is not implemented yet.

signModule.perFileModeHint: One PIN entry per file. Each file gets its own container that can be verified, and sent, entirely on its own.
signModule.pinInOwnWindow: The card middleware is asking for your signature PIN in its own window. This application never sees it.
